solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some editors may long to be this advanced

definitions.text: Some editors may long to be this

blocks.clueFragment: Some editors may long to be this
blocks.note: first meaning: a rival paper's editor would love to beat the famous London daily to a story
second meaning: more modern or progressive than one's own era

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads THE TIMES as the newspaper, which other editors hope to be in front of; the second is the ordinary idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea that is ahead of its era is progressive, so the idiom is a fair synonym for advanced.

clue.text: What you may do under a bishop? Pardon!

indicators.note: in a down entry, placing one part beneath another means it follows it in the grid

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess notation for a bishop
what a crossword solver does with this very clue

explanation.surface: A churchgoer asks what one does under a bishop, then begs forgiveness for a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: A B on top, SOLVE underneath, gives ABSOLVE: the clue addresses you, the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to forgive them formally, which is what a pardon does.

clue.text: Call for Congress to give leader the elbow

indicators.note: giving someone the elbow means getting rid of them, here the opening letter

blocks.note: congress in its sexual sense is a sex act

explanation.surface: A demand for Congress to sack its leader, as if American politics were on the agenda.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the American legislature, but it is used in its old sense of sexual union.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a payment is to demand or require it, so the verb matches call for.

clue.text: Condemn drop in value on one's release

indicators.note: when one is released it is let go, so that single letter leaves the word

blocks.note: to depreciate is to lose value

explanation.surface: A financial report condemns a fall in value after something is released.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (one) from DEPRECIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deprecate's older sense is to express strong disapproval of something, which is to condemn it.

clue.text: Alert to danger of Balls going to Greens?

definitions.text: Alert to danger of Balls going to Greens?

blocks.clueFragment: Alert to danger of Balls going to Greens?
blocks.note: surface reading: a warning that Ed Balls is defecting to the Green Party
setter's reading: golf balls flying towards the putting greens, prompting a golfer's shout

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest politics; the clue is really about the warning cry on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers shout this word to warn people in the path of a struck ball.

clue.text: A way to gate-crash hotel club in Aspen?

indicators.note: a gate-crasher pushes into a party, so these letters push inside the others

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Someone finds a way to gatecrash an exclusive hotel club in the Colorado ski resort of Aspen.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspen looks like the ski resort, but it is the tree; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is a broadleaf tree, and timber from broadleaf trees is classed as this, so aspen is an instance.

clue.text: One following others around royal route

indicators.note: around means wrapping one part about another

blocks.note: a tail follows someone closely
R is an abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A follower trails other people along a route taken by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or track, so it serves as a route.

clue.text: Spooner's said Oldman models bloomers

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

blocks.note: Oldman is the actor Gary Oldman, and models means moulds, giving Gary moulds; swap the first sounds

explanation.surface: Gary Oldman poses in women's old-fashioned knickers, according to Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' looks like underwear, but it means flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Marigolds are bright orange garden flowers, so they are bloomers in the cryptic sense of things that bloom.

clue.text: Austere hospital screening section

indicators.note: a screen surrounds and hides something, so one part encloses the other

blocks.note: SAN is short for sanatorium
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A bare, no-frills hospital is screening one section of its patients.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Spartans were famed for frugal discipline, so the adjective means severe and plain.

clue.text: Career MP out with son, lively little lad?

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A politician's career is over, along with his son, a lively young boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose and by example, as the question mark admits: a boisterous child is one who scampers about.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamperer is anyone who runs about playfully, and an energetic small boy is a typical example.

clue.text: A unit of old soldiers boarding vessel

indicators.note: people boarding a ship go inside it, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Territorial Army, the former name of Britain's Army Reserve
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A unit of veteran troops climbs aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a ship to be boarded, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, and arteries are blood vessels.

clue.text: Such as a superior that's left for the front

definitions.note: definition by example: a is one of these

indicators.note: putting one thing in place of the front means the opening character is swapped out

blocks.note: better means superior
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something like a superior who has been left in charge at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: L replaces the B of BETTER. The definition hides at the start: 'a' is an example of one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: The character a is the first in the alphabet, so it is one of these written symbols.

clue.text: Vampire book or The Remains of the Day?

blocks.note: first meaning: Stephenie Meyer's teenage vampire novel
second meaning, read literally: the last light left at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: The Remains of the Day is also a Kazuo Ishiguro novel, which makes the clue look like a choice between two books.
explanation.definitionFit: The faint light after sunset is what remains of the day, and the vampire saga bears the same title.

clue.text: Make beloved finish off peeled pears

indicators.note: peeling removes the skin, so the outermost letters are stripped off

blocks.note: the end is the finish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eats the last of the peeled pears to win affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them liked or loved by others.

clue.text: Note female cats leaving town — strays?

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so the letter for that word drops out

blocks.note: D is a musical note
tigresses are female big cats
T is an occasional abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: A note about female cats leaving town: are they strays?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strays' looks like a noun for homeless cats, but it is the verb: wanders off the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject, which is to stray from it.

clue.text: Singer taking large boy band on tour

indicators.note: a band on tour moves around, so the letters travel into a new order

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer takes a big boy band out on tour as his support act.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter famed for 'Blowin' in the Wind'.

clue.text: Break apart lettering advertising club?

definitions.note: the answer split as two words, DISCO HERE

blocks.note: first meaning: a rare verb for coming to pieces or losing cohesion
second meaning, split into two words: a sign pointing to a nightclub

explanation.walkthrough: A rare word, found in the big Oxford dictionaries but not Chambers; the question mark flags reading it as a two-word sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Discohere is formed like incoherent: to lose cohesion, so to fall to pieces or separate.

clue.text: Bug or second sickness caused by drink?

indicators.note: a sickness caused by something is named after its cause, so the cause comes first

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
wine is a drink
flu is a sickness

explanation.surface: Is it a bug, or a second bout of illness brought on by too much to drink?
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a hangover gets passed off as illness; the real definition is just 'Bug', an informal word for an infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug is informal for an infectious illness, and this pandemic influenza strain is one.

clue.text: Legal woe that's affected high-flyer

indicators.note: something affected has been changed, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A successful high-flyer has been hit by legal troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' looks like an ambitious executive, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle owl is a very large owl, and as a bird it flies high, so it is a literal high-flyer.

clue.text: One may be plucked by intellectual in Bow, say

indicators.note: say asks for the words as they are spoken rather than written

blocks.note: an intellectual is a highbrow; Bow is in London's East End, where Cockneys drop the H

explanation.surface: A brainy East Ender plucks something, as if a guitar or a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a Cockney district of East London, and Cockney speech drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: People pluck stray hairs from the arch of hair above the eye to shape it.

clue.text: Series of houses upgrading drains

indicators.note: a series is a run of consecutive items, here a run of consecutive letters across the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A row of houses being upgraded with new drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drains' looks like the plumbing being upgraded, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain resources is to exhaust or consume them completely.

clue.text: Grant-holding head for board of artists

indicators.note: holding means grasping something inside, so one part sits within the other

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the head
to let is to allow or grant

explanation.surface: An arts funding body headed by someone holding a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board of artists' looks like an arts committee, but it is the flat board a painter mixes colours on.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the thin board a painter holds to mix pigments on.

clue.text: Sport Gucci's latest in English clothing outlet

indicators.note: latest means the most recent, the final letter of the designer's name
clothing means dressing something, so letters wrap around the others

blocks.note: ENG is the abbreviation for English
the end of the fashion house's name
a vent is an outlet for air or steam

explanation.surface: Gucci's newest line appears in an English clothing shop.
explanation.walkthrough: It is a nested container: the designer's last letter goes in first, then the outlet goes inside that. 'Clothing outlet' reads as a shop but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the equestrian sport combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Support getting topless any minute

indicators.note: something topless has lost its top, which in a down entry is its first letter

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bra support goes missing as someone goes topless at any minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a unit of time with 'any', but it is the adjective meaning tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute pronounced my-NEWT means very small, and teeny is a childish word for tiny.

clue.text: See Liberals about fuss over nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one part goes round the other
turning something over flips it, so the whole is read backwards

blocks.note: L for Liberal, doubled with S to make it plural
ado is a fuss

explanation.surface: Look how the Liberal Democrats kick up a fuss over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Liberals is the plural of the abbreviation L, written with a doubled letter as pp is for pages. Sod all is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang phrase means absolutely nothing, as in 'he did sod all'.

clue.text: Very quiet beer outside The Empire?

indicators.note: outside means one part sits around the other

blocks.note: ale is a beer
pianissimo in music, marked pp

explanation.surface: A drink outside a pub or theatre called The Empire, said very quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Empire' tempts towards New York's Big Apple, but Empire is a variety of eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Empire is a red dessert variety of this fruit, so the definition is an example, flagged by the question mark.

clue.text: Extra capital on switching banks to Rotterdam

indicators.note: switching the banks swaps the letters at the edges of a word for others

blocks.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
the banks of this Dutch city's name are its outside letters

explanation.surface: Extra capital is moved from one bank to another in Rotterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and M of ROME change places, matching Rotterdam's outer letters in the new order M...R: ROME becomes MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: More means additional, which is the sense of extra.

clue.text: Hear blooming riveting woman in 40s?

indicators.note: hear asks the solver to listen to the word rather than read it

blocks.note: rosy means healthily pink, blooming

explanation.surface: Listen to a glowing, captivating woman in her forties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riveting' looks like fascinating, but it is literal: Rosie the Riveter was the 1940s American poster figure for women factory workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie the Riveter symbolised the women who worked in wartime munitions factories in the 1940s.

clue.text: Plant container of grass on fellow junior

indicators.note: in an across entry, one thing on another comes after it

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a junior is lower in rank
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A junior colleague keeps a pot of cannabis in a plant holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowerpot is the container a plant grows in.

clue.text: A holiday message Pink Floyd release

blocks.note: first meaning: the stock phrase written on a postcard
second meaning: the band's 1975 album

explanation.walkthrough: The 1975 album is a tribute to the band's former member Syd Barrett.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the classic line on a seaside postcard and also a Pink Floyd album title.
